rationale: Identity was properly verified via matching email. However, there are multiple policy and accuracy issues: (1) The agent changed both orders’ shipping addresses and the user default address without first stating the exact address to be applied and obtaining explicit confirmation of that exact change, as required by policy. The user only said to use the “current address on file,” and the agent did not restate the specific address before performing writes. (2) The agent also modified the user default address without explicit confirmation at that moment, and set it to the same address already on file, which may not reflect the user’s true new home. (3) Critically, when assisting with the tablet exchange to the cheapest option, the tool showed an available variant at $903.95 (item_id 2106335193) that was cheaper than the $941.03 option the agent selected. The agent incorrectly stated the $941.03 option was the cheapest and proceeded with that modification, resulting in an inaccurate recommendation and not fulfilling the user’s “cheapest” request. (4) The agent correctly handled that a pending order can’t be exchanged and offered a modification instead, with confirmation, and the refund amount matched the price difference. Nonetheless, the earlier confirmation and selection errors violate the pass criteria.
